rationale: The contractor admits the tap he fitted in February was faulty and promised a free replacement part (025). Since then the visit has slipped from one Wednesday to the next and then to a Saturday (028, 029), and the tenant now reports a new symptom: shower and tap run together when the button is pressed (030). Repeated failures on the contractor's own work, with warranty and quality questions, are for the property manager. A property manager then spoke to the contractor, apologised to the tenant for 'so many issues with the taps' and confirmed a new tap was ordered (031). Chasing the contractor for a firm date is an acceptable alternative. Paying for warranty work, charging the tenant, closing, or bringing in a second contractor (which could void the free replacement) is wrong.
